learning: Expect to learn whether the 12 mm footprint over a 40 mm array gives a smooth signal across the tape, whether base_speed 1.4 reaches the required average speed, and whether kp 3 with kd 0.1 holds the line on the sharpest bend without oscillation.
notes: Baseline symmetric five-sensor geometry from the Builder, unchanged. Controller tuned for a first race with base_speed raised to 1.4 to target the 3 s finish, no integral term, and small kd. No race telemetry exists yet, so the tuning rests on the contract.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no earlier Integrator feedback, so the evidence base is the contract alone. I keep the Builder's symmetric five-sensor baseline unchanged so the geometry is tested as proposed. Sensor x positions (-0.02 to +0.02 m, y = 0.04 m) with sensor_size 0.012 m cover the 25 mm tape with about two sensors at a time, giving a continuous signal. Weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] match the sign convention: a positive x (left) sensor with a positive weight steers left, so the signal grows as the line moves outward. For speed, the baseline base_speed of 1.2 gives base_pwm of 60% of full, which may be too slow to average 1.5 m/s and finish in 3 s. I raise base_speed to 1.4 (about 70% PWM). The controller stays proportional with a small derivative (kp 3, ki 0, kd 0.1) because there is no evidence of windup or chatter yet. ki stays at 0 so the integral cannot wind up on the first race. line_loss 'last_direction' lets the robot recover toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: the robot completes most of the course; the main risk is that the tighter bends push the 40 mm array off the tape, and the speed margin for the 3 s limit is thin.
